newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo says fears arrest.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo says fears arrest.

text.p: Argentina's former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo said Monday he feared begin made a political prisoner and accused hidden "mafias" of using the courts to protect themselves from corruption probes.

Cavallo told local radio an investigation into former Customs Service head Gustavo Parino -- a close associate of the one-time minister -- was an attack by corrupt interests within the state and that he might be next on the list.
When Parino is detained "he will become the first political prisoner" of the Argentine government, Cavallo said, adding, "I wouldn't be surprised if I were the second political prisoner."

Cavallo's latest volley in his fierce assault on alleged official corruption came just hours after he repeated charges that President Carlos Menem knew of bribes paid to officials to win a $250 million contract for U.S. firm IBM.

At a Sunday news conference, Cavallo said Menem's chief of staff Alberto Kohan covered up bribes to win the contract with state-owned Banco Nacion, and said "He should be in jail, the same as the the officials involved in the IBM-Banco Nacion affair."
Cavallo added "I think it likely that President Menem knew from Kohan's mouth that there were bribes paid."

Menem was present at a meeting with Cavallo in August 1995 when Kohan allegedly "made it understood" that one of his subordinates, Juan Carlos Cattaneo, had paid bribes in the 1993 deal, Cavallo said.
Kohan has denied the meeting took place.
Cavallo called the news conference after a judge announced Saturday that he was investigating Parino for alleged involvement in an enormous smuggling ring which infiltrated the customs service.
"The mafias have changed their strategy," Cavallo said, "In the past they used bombs and attcked people, and now they are opting, as has been demonstrated, for judicial harassment.

Since being sacked by Menem in July, Cavallo has peppered the government and judiciary with accusations of graft. He has at the same time been enmeshed in a series of court cases, including slander suits against him.
